conceptZh: 「川」的三筆化作三道河流，小鴨的大泳圈卡住，洩氣後才順利漂走。
object: A toy duck with an oversized inflatable ring and three blue river strokes
morph: An accurately formed 川 becomes a miniature river playground; its three solid blue strokes remain fixed while a toy duck floats along the middle stroke.
creativeAngle: 直接把正確字形當河道；小鴨的泳圈大到跨過三筆，洩氣後卻縮成迷你腰圈，以尺寸反差製造笑點，避免河流拉直後失去左撇。
promptEn:
Create an exactly 8-second animated toy comedy in a locked, straight-on overhead view. Center one correctly formed Traditional Chinese glyph 川, filling about 70% of frame height with generous margins, on a light warm-cream background. Use a faithful standard educational glyph silhouette in saturated solid blue: a gently left-falling first stroke and two separate upright strokes, preserving their correct lengths and spacing. These three unoutlined blue strokes serve as miniature rivers; their silhouettes stay fixed and readable throughout. All objects are visibly stylized animated toys.

At the opening, a tiny yellow toy duck floats near the upper end of the middle stroke inside an absurdly oversized coral inflatable ring spanning all three rivers. Its little paddle feet churn enthusiastically, but the ring rests across the dry gaps and goes nowhere. After a brief puzzled pause, at 2.3 seconds the duck taps the ring's valve. With a soft, comical squeak, the enormous ring deflates into a tiny snug waist ring; the duck bobs once in surprise, then glides down the middle river and exits below the frame by 4.4 seconds. Keep the whole glyph centered and uncropped, with no camera movement. From 4.4 through 8.0 seconds, hold the pristine solid-blue 川 completely still and unobstructed, with all props gone.

Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen voice speaks clear Taiwanese Mandarin, saying exactly “川、川、河川”. Say the first 川 around 0.5 seconds, the second around 1.6 seconds, and 河川 around 5.3 seconds during the clear final hold. Use the reading ㄔㄨㄢ for 川, natural pauses, and no further speech. Keep the gentle valve squeak below the voice; use no background music. Only the single target glyph 川 appears on screen; the vocabulary is audio only. No subtitles, other text, watermark, clutter, or flashing effects. Use soft toy lighting and bright, non-neon colors.

conceptZh: 太空人玩偶踩印章卻飄起來，翻個跟斗後用圓頭盔輕輕壓印，印出像河水流動的「川」。
object: One chunky unmarked printing stamp with a concealed river-blue ink face.
morph: A gentle helmet-first landing presses the stamp; lifting it reveals 川, with brief downstream ripples inside its three strokes before the ink becomes completely solid.
creativeAngle: 改用失重蓋章的肢體笑點：越想用力踩，自己越往上飄，最後意外靠頭盔壓印成功。印面預先固定正確字形，避免把第一筆錯畫成直線；水紋只在筆畫內流動，連結河川意象。
promptEn:
Create an exactly 8-second stylized 3D toy animation with one original, eager astronaut toy wearing a transparent fishbowl helmet, a peach-colored molded suit, oversized boots, and a simple cartoon face. Its personality is proudly determined, but it keeps floating upward at inconvenient moments. The only supporting object is a chunky, unmarked printing stamp. Use a locked, slightly elevated frontal view of a pale cream printing surface, with bright, soft lighting and clear spatial staging.

At the opening, the stamp rests over the central printing area. The small astronaut stands on its broad top, confidently preparing to stomp. At 0.6 seconds it pushes down with both boots—but its boots slowly leave the stamp instead. It looks down, astonished, then pedals furiously in midair while the stamp remains stubbornly still. Its oversized boots carry it through one slow half-somersault. After a tiny suspended pause, it gently drops helmet-first onto the stamp at 2.5 seconds: a soft hollow 'ponk' presses the stamp, and the toy’s springy legs wobble overhead. Keep this clearly a harmless plastic-toy bounce. The astronaut blinks, realizes the accident worked, rights itself, and proudly lifts the stamp. Its renewed upward drift carries both toy and stamp diagonally out of the printing area by 4.2 seconds.

The lifted stamp reveals exactly one correctly formed Traditional Chinese 川, centered, uncropped, and approximately 70% of frame height with generous margins. Construct the concealed stamp face to produce the correct readable impression: a leftmost stroke that descends and gently sweeps left, a shorter upright middle stroke, and a longer upright right stroke, with clear open gaps. Never show the stamp’s underside or a second glyph. During the reveal, subtle darker-blue ripples travel downward entirely within the three ink strokes, suggesting flowing river water without altering their contours. The ripples settle by 4.6 seconds into saturated, uniformly solid blue. Hold this pristine, unobstructed glyph completely still from 4.6 to 8.0 seconds.

A warm, friendly off-screen voice speaks clear Taiwanese Mandarin, saying exactly “川、川、河川”: the first 川 at approximately 4.3 seconds, the second at 5.3 seconds, and 河川 at 6.5 seconds. Pronounce 川 as ㄔㄨㄢ, with relaxed pauses, and stop after the word. Keep the finished glyph visible throughout the spoken sequence. Use only quiet floating and plastic-contact sound effects beneath the voice, with no music. The single 川 impression is the only visible text; keep the vocabulary audio-only. No subtitles, logos, watermark, clutter, camera movement, or flashing effects.
